title: Rinnai Process — Basic
sourceNote: Zero-knowledge playbook. Plain English. No portal passwords or payment credentials.
intro: Assume no prior process or product knowledge. Examples are in brackets. Try the Spare Parts Bible and this Process desk first.

chapters.title: 1. What this job is
chapters.blurb: Zone Contractor role in one page.
body: MTC is a Rinnai Zone Contractor. That means: we do Rinnai service jobs, we close them in Rinnai’s online system (the partner portal), and we bill Rinnai and/or the customer depending on warranty.
You do not need to remember any of that history. Follow the steps in this Process desk for each job.
If something is unclear, use this Process desk and the Spare Parts Bible (pins + search). Do not guess model numbers or part numbers.

chapters.title: 2. Open the job in the portal
chapters.blurb: Work Order arrival, plate, notes, submit.
body: Open the Rinnai partner portal in your browser (bookmark / link from IT — the password is never stored in this Bible).
Find the Work Order (WO) for this job. A Work Order is Rinnai’s ticket for one visit / one unit [example: an 8-digit Rinnai Work Order number, not the SA (service appointment) number].
On the Work Order, log that someone arrived and that JSA (job safety assessment) was done, if your process asks for it.
Enter the unit’s model and serial from the metal data plate on the unit (tech photo if you are not on site). Do not invent a model from memory — see chapter 9 Data plates.
Add completion notes (what was done). Add photos if Rinnai/MTC asks for them.
Submit the Work Order for Rinnai to review when the visit is finished.

chapters.title: 3. Parts on the Work Order
chapters.blurb: Real part codes only — Bible first.
body: If parts were used or need ordering, you need a real part number [usually 8 digits, e.g. 92099423].
Look it up in this Spare Parts Bible: Pin 1 (type of system) → Pin 2 (series) → Pin 3 (exact unit) → search. Example series: HD / HDC continuous flow [e.g. HD200, HD28, HDC32].
If the tech wrote a number on the job sheet, check it in the Bible against that unit before you submit it on the Work Order.
If stores hold the physical part, confirm the code on the bag/box still matches the Bible result for that unit.
In the portal Work Order, open RELATED → Parts and Labour → New. Put the part code into Price Book Entry (same idea as labour codes). Save.
Mark whether it is warranty or chargeable (customer pays). Wrong choice = wrong who pays — use chapter 8 Warranty, or switch to Detailed for the full tables and the quick assess checker.
If the part is not a Rinnai stock part (third-party), use the chargeable / markup rules in chapter 5 Chargeable & PayWay — do not invent a customer price from Bible Net alone.
If the Bible cannot find a purchaseable part, use Flag problem on the part card (or note on the Work Order) — do not guess a code.

chapters.title: 4. Labour on the Work Order
chapters.blurb: Hours and labour codes on the Work Order.
body: Add labour time the tech was on site (hours) using the labour codes listed in Detailed Process → Labour [examples used today: A15 for many domestic-style jobs, CFA for many commercial-style jobs].
Labour also goes under RELATED → Parts and Labour on the Work Order.

chapters.title: 5. If the customer must pay (chargeable)
body: If work or parts are not covered by warranty, the customer pays MTC (then we still settle with Rinnai as required).
Give a written quote. Get signed acceptance before you chase payment.
Collect via PayWay (or the current MTC card/payment process). If they refuse to pay, follow the refusal path written in Detailed Process → Chargeable & PayWay — do not invent a new path.
Issue a receipt if needed.

chapters.title: 6. Invoice Rinnai in Exo (code RSW)
chapters.blurb: Accounts job code and payment track.
body: Exo is MTC’s accounts system. Invoice Rinnai using job code RSW (Rinnai Service Work) unless Detailed Process lists a different current code.
Match labour and parts to what you entered on the portal Work Order.
Track payment on the RCTI (recipient-created tax invoice) / payment tracker path written in Detailed Process (keep the path current in Process — do not rely on memory of old year folders).
Leave the job open in your checklist until Rinnai has paid / closed their side.

chapters.title: 7. Finished goods (replace the whole unit)
chapters.blurb: Whole heater, not a spare part.
body: Sometimes the unit is dead and Rinnai/MTC replace the whole heater — that is a finished good, not a spare part.
Use the Zone Contractor Hot Water price list (unit/package list) — not the spare-parts Net prices in this Bible.
Raise a Finished Goods request using the steps in {{link:detailed:fg}}Detailed Process → Finished goods{{/link}}. Confirm the exact model code from the data plate + that price list before ordering.

chapters.title: 8. Is it still under warranty?
chapters.blurb: Five gates + quick tool — escalate greys to Rinnai.
body: Age the job from the install date (or dataplate manufacture date + 2 months if install is unknown). Parts years and labour years are separate.

Walk five gates: (1) still in period, (2) compliant install, (3) correct application, (4) water in-spec, (5) clear Rinnai factory fault vs site/external. Grey or disputed at gate 5 → escalate to Rinnai — never “chase the booklet.”
Domestic vs commercial depends on the family °C limit: gas continuous flow / Demand Duo pack ≤65°C; Hotflo / heat pump / solar ≤70°C; Efinity ≤60°C.
Use This quick tool can help you assess below. It suggests labour+parts, parts only, chargeable, or escalate to Rinnai (with a plain-English path summary + phone checklist).
Full year tables: {{link:detailed:warranty}}Detailed Process → Warranty{{/link}}. Desk aid only — if Rinnai disagrees later, follow the Work Order close-off.

chapters.title: 9. Reading the data plate
chapters.blurb: So Pin 3 and portal model are right.
body: Find the metal plate on the unit (tech photo is fine).
Read the model line [often starts with REU-… or a marketing name like HD200e].
Read the serial number.
Type those into the portal asset fields. In the Bible, match Pin 3 to that plate — never guess.

chapters.title: 10. When you are stuck
chapters.blurb: Bible + Process first; ask if needed.
body: First: use this Process desk + the Spare Parts Bible (pins, search, Flag problem). Do not guess.
No part number: Pin the unit in the Bible and search by what failed [fan, heat exchanger, valve…]. Use Flag problem if nothing purchaseable shows.
Plate unreadable / two possible units: get a clearer photo of the plate from the tech; do not pick a Pin 3 at random.
Warranty vs chargeable unclear: open chapter 8 Is it still under warranty? and run the quick assess tool, then use the outcome on the Work Order charge type.
Portal login / password: use IT’s password process (never store passwords in this Bible).
Try the Spare Parts Bible and this Process desk first. Still stuck? Ask your supervisor or manager. For parts lookups or incoming warranties, you can also ask Beau for a second opinion.
